\item The canonical comparison of P4.12 gives
$K_T+D\equiv0$, with $D$ effective. We first determine the
reduced conductor as an embedded topological space; this
step does not require the ruling to descend to $S$.
Let $\pi:T\to T_0$ be the sequence of point blowdowns to

guards.literal_new:
\item Proposition~\ref{cdp:st:A.5.3}, with the identity as the
minimal resolution of the smooth surface $T$, gives
$\omega_T(D)\simeq\nu^*\omega_S$ with $D$ effective and with its
conductor multiplicities. Proposition~\ref{night:P4.12} makes this
line torsion, so $K_T+D\equiv0$.
Let $\pi:T\to T_0$ be the sequence of point blowdowns to the
minimal ruled surface $r_0:T_0\to B$, and put $D_0=\pi_*D$.
By \cite[III.10, p.~40]{Beauville1978}, write $T_0=\mathbf P_B(V)$
for a rank-two bundle $V$ on $B$. In the basis of the tautological
class $h=c_1(\OO_{\mathbf P_B(V)}(1))$ and the fibre class $F$,
$h^2=\deg V$, $h\cdot F=1$, $F^2=0$ and
$K_{T_0}=-2h+(\deg V+2g-2)F$
\cite[III.18, pp.~46--47]{Beauville1978}.
Thus $K_{T_0}+D_0\equiv0$ and $D_0\cdot F=2$.
guards.reason: Give the exact conductor and ruled-surface formulas in the opened primary basis.
guards.mathematical_transport: The resolution is the identity, h=nu; pi pushes the effective conductor to D0. The projective-bundle basis has K.F=-2 and fixes the degree-two horizontal part. No descent morphism from S to the ruling base is introduced.

A surface factor of genus at least two cannot occur
in a virtually abelian group, by the finite-cover
argument of P4R.2.
guards.literal_new:
A genus-$h$ surface factor with $h\ge2$ cannot be virtually
abelian: a connected degree-$d$ cover has genus $1+d(h-1)>1$,
and its fundamental group is nonabelian. Projection onto this
surface factor is a quotient map, while every quotient of a
virtually abelian group is virtually abelian.
guards.reason: Give the exact surface-group quotient and covering calculation.
